description: Subscription creation and update for NF status notifications, including same-PLMN, different-PLMN, and forwarding/redirecting NRF cases.

constraints.statement: The NF Service Consumer shall send a POST request to the resource URI representing the "subscriptions" collection resource to create an NF status subscription.
evidence: "The NF Service Consumer shall send a POST request to the resource URI representing the \"subscriptions\" collection resource."
constraints.why_interesting: This defines the required HTTP method and target resource for subscription creation.

constraints.statement: The request body shall include the data indicating the type of notifications the NF Service Consumer is interested in receiving.
evidence: "The request body shall include the data indicating the type of notifications that the NF Service Consumer is interested in receiving"
constraints.why_interesting: This is a required request payload element that can be validated by API tests.

constraints.statement: The request body shall contain a callback URI where the NF Service Consumer shall be prepared to receive the notification.
evidence: "it also contains a callback URI, where the NF Service Consumer shall be prepared to receive the actual notification from the NRF"
constraints.why_interesting: Callback URI presence is essential for notification delivery and is testable in request validation.

constraints.statement: If the NF Service Consumer creates multiple subscriptions in the NRF, it should use distinct callback URIs for each subscription.
evidence: "When the NF Service Consumer creates multiple subscriptions in the NRF, it should use distinct callback URIs for each subscription."
constraints.why_interesting: This is a behavioral recommendation, but not normative enough to keep as a constraint.

constraints.statement: The subscription shall be authorized or rejected by the NRF by checking the relevant input attributes in the subscription request body against the list of authorization attributes in the NF Profile of the target NF Instance to be monitored.
evidence: "The subscription shall be authorized, or rejected, by the NRF by checking the relevant input attributes ... against the list of authorization attributes in the NF Profile of the target NF Instance to be monitored."
constraints.why_interesting: This defines the authorization decision rule for subscription creation.

constraints.statement: If the requesting entity is not authorized to subscribe to the complete profile of NF instances, the NRF shall reject the request or handle it as a subscription request without access to the complete profile.
evidence: "If the requesting entity is not authorized to do so, the NRF shall reject the request or handle it as a subscription request without access to the complete profile."
constraints.why_interesting: This constrains NRF behavior when complete-profile access is unauthorized.

constraints.statement: When the subscription request is for a set of NFs and some NF Instances are not authorized for the NF Service Consumer, those NF Instances shall not trigger any notification event from the NRF to the NF Service Consumer.
evidence: "the NF Instances in the set that are not authorized for the NF Service Consumer that requested the subscription, shall not result in triggering any notification event from the NRF to the NF Service Consumer."
constraints.why_interesting: This is a precise negative notification rule for partially authorized subscriptions.

constraints.statement: On successful subscription creation, the NRF shall return 201 Created.
evidence: "On success, \"201 Created\" shall be returned."
constraints.why_interesting: This is the required success status code for subscription creation.

constraints.statement: On successful subscription creation, the response shall contain the data related to the created subscription, including the validity time determined by the NRF.
evidence: "The response shall contain the data related to the created subscription, including the validity time, as determined by the NRF"
constraints.why_interesting: This specifies required response content on success.

constraints.statement: After the subscription expires, the NF Service Consumer shall create a new subscription in the NRF if it wants to keep receiving status notifications.
evidence: "Once the subscription expires, if the NF Service Consumer wants to keep receiving status notifications, it shall create a new subscription in the NRF."
constraints.why_interesting: This is a state-transition rule for expired subscriptions.

constraints.statement: If subscription creation fails due to errors in the SubscriptionData JSON object in the request body, the NRF shall return 400 Bad Request with ProblemDetails.
evidence: "If the creation of the subscription fails at the NRF due to errors in the SubscriptionData JSON object in the request body, the NRF shall return \"400 Bad Request\" status code with the ProblemDetails IE providing details of the error."
constraints.why_interesting: This is a specific client-error mapping for malformed subscription data.

constraints.statement: If verification of the subscription request against the NF service consumer certificate is unsuccessful, the request shall be rejected with 400 Bad Request and the cause attribute set to INVALID_CLIENT.
evidence: "If the verification is unsuccessful, the request shall be rejected with \"400 Bad Request\" status code and the \"cause\" attribute set to \"INVALID_CLIENT\"."
constraints.why_interesting: This is a concrete authorization/validation failure response that can be tested.

constraints.statement: If subscription creation fails due to NRF internal errors, the NRF shall return 500 Internal Server Error with ProblemDetails.
evidence: "If the creation of the subscription fails at the NRF due to NRF internal errors, the NRF shall return \"500 Internal Server Error\" status code with the ProblemDetails IE providing details of the error."
constraints.why_interesting: This defines the server-error response for internal failures.

constraints.statement: In the case of redirection, the NRF shall return a 3xx status code containing a Location header with a URI pointing to another NRF service instance.
evidence: "In the case of redirection, the NRF shall return 3xx status code, which shall contain a Location header with an URI pointing to the endpoint of another NRF service instance."
constraints.why_interesting: This is a required redirect behavior and header requirement.

constraints.statement: For subscription creation in a different PLMN, the POST request sent to the NRF in the Serving PLMN shall include the identity of the Home PLMN in the SubscriptionData parameter.
evidence: "this request shall include the identity of the PLMN of the home NRF in the SubscriptionData parameter in the request body."
constraints.why_interesting: This is a required cross-PLMN request field.

constraints.statement: If the NRF in the Serving PLMN knows that OAuth2-based authorization is required for accessing the NFManagement service of the NRF in the Home PLMN and the request does not include an access token, the NRF in the Serving PLMN may reject the request with 401 Unauthorized.
evidence: "if the request received at the NRF in the Serving PLMN does not include an access token, the NRF in the Serving PLMN may reject the request with a 401 Unauthorized"
constraints.why_interesting: This is an authorization-related conditional response, though expressed with MAY rather than SHALL.

constraints.statement: On successful cross-PLMN subscription creation, the NRF in the Serving PLMN shall generate a new subscriptionID and send it to the NF Service Consumer.
evidence: "a new subscriptionID shall be generated by the NRF in the Serving PLMN ... and shall be sent to the NF Service Consumer in the Serving PLMN."
constraints.why_interesting: This is a required identifier transformation for cross-PLMN subscriptions.

constraints.statement: If the Home NRF is located in a PLMN, the NRF in the Serving PLMN shall send a subscriptionID of the form <MCC>+<MNC>+"-"+<OriginalSubscriptionID> to the NF Service Consumer.
evidence: "If the Home NRF is located in a PLMN: The NRF in Serving PLMN ... shall send to the NF Service Consumer ... a subscriptionID that shall consist on the following structure: <MCC>+<MNC>+\"-\"+<OriginalSubscriptionID>"
constraints.why_interesting: This is a precise, testable formatting rule for returned subscription IDs.

constraints.statement: If the Home NRF is located in an SNPN, the NRF in the Serving PLMN shall send a subscriptionID of the form <MCC>+<MNC>+"-"+"x3Lf57A"+":nid="+<NID>+":"+<OriginalSubscriptionID> to the NF Service Consumer.
evidence: "If the Home NRF is located in an SNPN: <MCC>+<MNC>+\"-\"+\"x3Lf57A\"+\":nid=\"+<NID>+\":\"+<OriginalSubscriptionID>"
constraints.why_interesting: This is a precise, testable formatting rule for SNPN subscription IDs.

constraints.statement: The NRF in the Serving PLMN shall not keep state for a subscription created in a different PLMN.
evidence: "The NRF in Serving PLMN should not keep state for this created subscription"
constraints.why_interesting: This is a cross-PLMN state-handling rule, but it is expressed with SHOULD rather than SHALL.

constraints.statement: The Location header URI returned by the NRF in the Serving PLMN shall contain the modified subscriptionId, and if it is an absolute URI, its apiRoot shall point to the address of the NRF in the Serving PLMN.
evidence: "The URI in the Location header that the NRF in Serving PLMN returns ... shall contain a <subscriptionId> modified as described above and, if it is as an absolute URI, an apiRoot pointing to the address of the NRF in Serving PLMN."
constraints.why_interesting: This constrains both the Location header content and the apiRoot for cross-PLMN creation responses.

constraints.statement: The subscriptionId attribute in the response body returned by the NRF in the Serving PLMN shall also contain the modified subscriptionId.
evidence: "The subscriptionId attribute in the message body that the NRF in Serving PLMN returns ... shall also contain a <subscriptionId> modified as described above."
constraints.why_interesting: This is a required response-body identifier transformation.

constraints.statement: For subscription update, the NF Service Consumer shall send a PATCH request to the individual subscription resource URI received in the Location header of the successful 201 Created response.
evidence: "It is invoked by issuing an HTTP PATCH request on the URI representing the individual resource received in the Location header field of the \"201 Created\" response received during a successful subscription"
constraints.why_interesting: This defines the required update method and target resource.

constraints.statement: The PATCH request content shall contain a replace operation on the validityTime attribute of the SubscriptionData structure and shall contain a new suggested value for it.
evidence: "The content of the PATCH request shall contain a \"replace\" operation on the \"validityTime\" attribute of the SubscriptionData structure and shall contain a new suggested value for it"
constraints.why_interesting: This is a precise request-body requirement for subscription updates.

constraints.statement: No other attribute of the subscription resource shall be updated as part of the PATCH operation.
evidence: "no other attribute of the resource shall be updated as part of this operation."
constraints.why_interesting: This is a negative constraint on update scope.

constraints.statement: If the NRF accepts the extension of the subscription lifetime and accepts the requested validityTime value, it shall return 204 No Content.
evidence: "if the NRF accepts the extension of the lifetime of the subscription, and it accepts the requested value for the \"validityTime\" attribute, a response with status code \"204 No Content\" shall be returned."
constraints.why_interesting: This is the required success status when the requested validity time is accepted.

constraints.statement: If the NRF accepts the extension of the subscription lifetime but assigns a validity time different from the suggested value, it shall return 200 OK.
evidence: "if the NRF accepts the extension of the lifetime of the subscription, but it assigns a validity time different than the value suggested by the NF Service Consumer, a \"200 OK\" response code shall be returned."
constraints.why_interesting: This distinguishes the response code based on whether the requested validity time is honored.

constraints.statement: When returning 200 OK for a subscription update, the response shall contain the new subscription resource representation including the new validity time determined by the NRF.
evidence: "The response shall contain the new resource representation of the \"subscription\" resource, which includes the new validity time, as determined by the NRF"
constraints.why_interesting: This is a required response-body content rule for partial acceptance of the update.

constraints.statement: If subscription update fails due to errors in the JSON Patch object in the request body, the NRF shall return 400 Bad Request with ProblemDetails.
evidence: "If the update of the subscription fails at the NRF due to errors in the JSON Patch object in the request body, the NRF shall return \"400 Bad Request\" status code with the ProblemDetails IE providing details of the error."
constraints.why_interesting: This is a specific client-error mapping for malformed patch requests.

constraints.statement: If subscription update fails due to NRF internal errors, the NRF shall return 500 Internal Server Error with ProblemDetails.
evidence: "If the update of the subscription fails at the NRF due to NRF internal errors, the NRF shall return \"500 Internal Server Error\" status code with the ProblemDetails IE providing details of the error."
constraints.why_interesting: This defines the server-error response for update failures.

constraints.statement: For subscription update in a different PLMN, the PATCH request sent to the NRF in the Serving PLMN shall include the identity of the Home NRF PLMN or SNPN as component values of the subscriptionID.
evidence: "this request shall include the identity of the PLMN or SNPN of the home NRF (MCC/MNC/NID values) as a component values of the susbcriptionID."
constraints.why_interesting: This is a required cross-PLMN identifier encoding rule for update requests.

constraints.statement: When forwarding a cross-PLMN subscription update to the NRF in the Home PLMN, the subscriptionID sent to the Home PLMN shall not contain the PLMN identity and shall be the same value as originally generated by the Home PLMN.
evidence: "the subscriptionID sent to the NRF in the Home PLMN shall not contain the identity of the PLMN (i.e., it shall be the same subscriptionID value as originally generated by the NRF in the Home PLMN)."
constraints.why_interesting: This is a precise forwarding rule for preserving the original home subscription ID.

constraints.statement: If the subscription was created in a different NRF in the HPLMN, the NRF receiving the update request shall forward the request toward the NRF in the HPLMN holding the subscription using the information included in the subscriptionID.
evidence: "the latter shall forward the request received from the NRF in the serving PLMN towards the NRF in the HPLMN holding the subscription, using the information included in the subscriptionID"
constraints.why_interesting: This is a required routing behavior for cross-PLMN updates.

constraints.statement: If the subscription update is redirected, the NRF shall return a 3xx status code containing a Location header with a URI pointing to another NRF service instance.
evidence: "In the case of redirection, the NRF shall return 3xx status code, which shall contain a Location header with an URI pointing to the endpoint of another NRF service instance."
constraints.why_interesting: This is a required redirect behavior for update operations.
